medium.title: Yen Wobbles Near 40-Year Low as Dollar Pauses for Breath
medium.summary:
The Japanese Yen is hovering near a 40-year low against the USD following U.S. inflation data that came in broadly in line with expectations, prompting traders to pare back bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes. Mixed signals from Fed officials have added to uncertainty around the policy path, keeping the dollar supported but momentarily pausing its advance. The DXY remains on track for its first back-to-back weekly gain since February, reflecting underlying dollar strength. **Relevance for INR traders:** A broadly strong dollar environment is a headwind for the Rupee, as it typically pressures EM currencies via risk-off sentiment and capital outflow dynamics. However, the scaling-back of aggressive Fed hike expectations offers some relief — if markets firm up a "Fed pause" narrative, INR could find near-term support. Watch for upcoming Fed speaker commentary and U.S. jobs/PCE data which will be the next key catalyst for USD direction and, by extension, INR/USD.

medium.title: Oil Prices Dive as More Tankers Move Through Strait of Hormuz
medium.summary: Crude oil prices are falling sharply and heading for steep weekly losses as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz normalises, alleviating earlier supply disruption fears. Despite a cargo vessel being struck near Oman — with suspected Iranian involvement — oil continues to flow uninterrupted. Analysts are flagging an emerging oversupply dynamic, with Saudi Aramco resuming loading operations adding further downward pressure on prices. **INR relevance:** Falling crude is materially positive for the Indian Rupee and the broader macro picture. India imports approximately 85% of its crude requirements, so lower oil prices compress the import bill, narrow the current account deficit, and reduce imported inflation pressure. This gives the RBI greater policy flexibility and reduces the need for FX reserve intervention to defend the Rupee. Bond markets should also take note — softer crude supports lower CPI prints, reinforcing the case for easing or a prolonged pause in the rate cycle. Watch Brent closely; sustained weakness below $70/bbl would be a meaningful tailwind for INR and G-Secs.

medium.title: Gold Gains as Dollar Weakens; Still on Track for Fourth Straight Weekly Loss
medium.summary: Gold prices edged modestly higher on Friday, supported by a softening US dollar and slightly reduced expectations of aggressive US interest rate hikes following the latest inflation data release. However, despite this intraday bounce, gold remains on course for its fourth consecutive weekly decline, having touched a seven-month low earlier in the week. Analysts attribute the sustained weakness to the inverse relationship between gold and the elevated interest rate environment. **INR/macro relevance:** A weaker US dollar, if sustained, is broadly constructive for emerging market currencies including the INR, as it reduces dollar demand pressure and can support FPI inflows into Indian assets. The easing of US rate-hike expectations is also a positive signal for Indian bond markets, as it reduces the interest rate differential risk that typically drives FPI outflows from G-Secs. Monitor the DXY trajectory and upcoming US Fed commentary for confirmation of this dollar softening trend.
